_source: Extracted from three real generated diet plans (deepak-sharma, anjali-joshi week1 PDFs) — every entry's exchangeType/servingRawG/exchangeUnits verified by reproducing the plans' exact per-meal kcal/protein/carbs/fat sums against Table 4.1's constants. See CLAUDE.md 'The exchange system'. south_indian (Malayali/Kerala), punjabi, gujarati, bengali, rajasthani and hyderabadi rows added separately, without a real generated-plan PDF to reverse-engineer — classified onto the same Table 4.1 exchange types and gram equivalences a dietitian would use (batter/flour flatbreads and steamed-rice items = cereal at 20 g raw per exchange, matching Roti/Rice; dal preparations and besan/gram-flour dishes = pulse at 30 g raw, matching Chana/Toor dal; paneer = meat at 40 g, matching Egg's convention for a protein-dense vegetarian option; regional cooking oils = fat at 5 g/exchange like Ghee/Mustard oil; spiced buttermilk preparations = milk_skim at 320 g, matching Curd/Taak). A few existing foods (Ghee, Bajra/Jowar bhakri, Mustard oil, Groundnut oil, Brinjal, Drumstick) had their regions widened rather than duplicated, where the same food is genuinely shared across cuisines (e.g. ghee in both north_indian and punjabi cooking). Macros are never invented per food — they still come from Table 4.1 by exchange type regardless of which specific food fills the slot. Round 2 (seasonal eligibility, see CLAUDE.md 'Seasonal eligibility'): confirmed against the LIVE foods table (not just this file — Aloo/Gobi/Methi/Mooli Paratha etc. were seeded via a separate migration, not this JSON) that meat_lean/meat/vegetable_b/fat pools for Punjab non-vegetarian were genuinely thin (2/1/2/1 distinct foods respectively) before adding real preparation-name aliases (Chicken curry/Tandoori chicken/Tandoori fish/Egg bhurji/Egg curry) and widening Carrot/Green peas/Onion/Mustard oil's regions to include punjabi (same shared-cuisine reasoning as the pass above) plus new Sweet corn/Radish/Dal makhani/Sprouts/Tori/Karela/Gobi rows. `seasons` retagging is scoped to only the foods with a concrete claim behind it (Sarson saag/Methi/Palak/Carrot -> winter, Lauki/Tinda/Guava -> monsoon, Musk melon -> summer) — every other region stays at the all_year default rather than getting fabricated seasonal tags with no source to check them against.
